newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unisource says net move further cements alliance.
newsitem.headline: Unisource says net move further cements alliance.

text.p: Unisource NV said on Wednesday its agreement to merge the international telecoms networks of its partners Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT cemented the alliance better than a share swap.

"What's happening here is that vital operations of the shareholders are combined together, they're transferring them, and of course this is the strongest binding factor you can imagine, stronger than swapping shares because you swap them back or sell them out," Unisource president and chief executive Paul Smits said in a telephone interview.
"It's a striking event which is now occurring, which after several months is impossible to redo. There is no return ticket from here," said Smits.

He said the move had not been specifically linked to Telefonica's exit from the Unisource partnership in April. Telefonica of Spain was asked to leave Unisource after news it had linked up with Concert, a rival business telecoms alliance between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp.
"This is part of an overall master plan which has several steps," said Smits.
He said Unisource was putting the Telefonica incident behind it and, although it had talked to potential partners, it was not in a hurry to cement a new link.
"We are not desperately seeking a fourth partner. It's a pity the Telefonica thing happened but that's that," said Smits.

"Unisource...is doing its act, it's growing tremendously, at the same time with or without Telefonica, discussions were underway with further partners on the European scene and maybe or maybe not this will lead to a new partner but the liklihood of that is limited I would say." -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
